thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx rate detected from private-vpc egress (eu-west-1). Multiple gateway 504/502 spikes. Paging on-call: @SRE Rotation. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/boards/egress-errors

Maya S: seeing the same, started ~12:34 UTC. errorRate jumped from ~0.3% -> ~12%. majority 504 gateway_timeouts from inference-gateway -> private-egress.

Ravi K: I'm on it. can someone check NAT metrics (ActiveConnections, EphemeralPortUsage, PortAllocationFailures)? I'll pull conntrack.

Jun Park: NAT logs show ephemeral port counters skyrocketing — ephemeral_port_used ~65530/65535 on transit-nat-1. lots of SYN_RECV states.

Elena V: any recent SG or firewall changes? i rolled a fw policy at 12:20 but targeted public egress only.

Maya S: no SG changes for private subnets. we did see a peering route flap at 12:28 that briefly self-healed. could be correlated.

Ravi K: running quick curl test from affected subnet, getting intermittent resets. sample logs:
```
12:36:02 UTC curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
12:36:03 UTC tcpdump: 10.2.3.4 -> 52.46.12.7 RST
```

SRE Rotation: taking pager. @Ravi, can we scale the NAT or fail over egress while we debug?

Jun Park: autoscale is enabled but config is min=1, max=3. current=1. we can bump to 3 but new instances take ~60s. immediate option: change route to backup-transit to relieve transit-nat pressure.

Maya S: customer impact note: 8 private deployments showing increased retry rates, a few user-facing timeouts reported. not all tenants affected; long-lived upstream connections hit worst.

Ravi K: routing fallback in progress — switching route table rtb-0abc from transit-nat-1 -> transit-nat-2: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id i-transit-2` (applying)

Elena V: also bumping conntrack limit on transit appliance: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000` and clearing stale entries per runbook. applying now.

SRE Rotation: after route switch + conntrack bump, metrics show error rate falling: 12:36 -> 12:38 dropped to ~2% and p95 latency improving. keep scaling NAT to 2 as steady state.

Jun Park: NAT pool returned to healthy: ephemeral_port_used < 10% after scaled instance and route shift. conntrack states trimmed ~30%.

Maya S: hypothesis: bursty client connection churn + a peering route transient led to SNAT ephemeral port churn and connection resets on transit appliance, causing gateway 504s.

Ravi K: immediate actions: set NAT autoscale min=2, add alert: ephemeral_port_used > 70% for 2m, enable port-preserving SNAT where feasible, and schedule follow-up to review peering BGP stability.

Elena V: filing customer-impact summary and notifying affected accounts (A, B, C). sending comms draft to support.

SRE Rotation: creating incident channel #inc-2418765432 and drafting postmortem. handoff to next oncall at 08:00 UTC tomorrow.

Maya S: thanks everyone — monitoring for 6h, will update if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:
